system.name: FL-UAV Swarm IDS
system.subtitle: Federated learning · CNN+LSTM network intrusion detection · Onboard edge IDS window features
system.tensor: 16×46 per sample: 44 wireless/network features + 2 synthetic telemetry channels (battery, CPU)

theatres.scene: Urban-core electromagnetic clutter: dense Wi‑Fi/BT and AP diversity; this FL round stresses DDoS / brute-force-like bursts embedded in high-volume legitimate traffic on edge IDS sliding windows.

Khartoum-area relay UAVs over arid corridors: mixed reconnaissance and scanning traffic with sporadic UDP-flooding bursts; this round stresses long-range lossy backhaul and heterogeneous client shards.
Urban–mountain fringe patrol: IDS windows under intermittent GNSS multipath and elevated RF interference; this round emphasizes jamming / de-authentication patterns on narrowband UAV relay links.

glossary.body: (1) UAV edge clients: three DroneClient instances (client.py) over gRPC to Flower; local CNN+LSTM trains on each train_split and returns parameter deltas. (2) Federated server: FedAvg aggregation and centralized IDS evaluation on test.npz. (3) RL trust bridge: builds client states from telemetry, local eval, global loss/precision, outputs trust scores. (4) APC: fuses threat, mission criticality, trust, and resources to emit next-round participate / noise_scale / freq_n, pushed to clients via server fit config—closing the loop.

On the Workflow page, one button calls /api/uav-workflow via dashboard/serve.py, which runs uav_workflow_sim: reads data/swarm_processed/test.npz, runs CnnLstmIDS forward (loads checkpoints/fl_global_last.pt if present; otherwise random-init demo weights). Alerts use softmax argmax vs a calibrated no-alert class. Then AdaptivePrivacyController outputs participate / noise_scale / freq_n. The UI shows a trimmed field set (scenario_side/tag, predicted_class, uplink fields); noisy aggregates and duplicate timestamps are hidden.
Three anchored theatres (Beijing, Sudan, Tehran) with WGS84 and narrative for maps and logs; IDS tensors and cleaning steps are described on the Dataset tab.
The server runs one forward pass of the current global model on the pooled global holdout test.npz. It reflects post-aggregation IDS quality on unseen pooled data, unlike per-client local eval.
Mean over test windows of battery SOC, CPU usage, etc. Summarizes fleet load/energy context; not a class label but can be read alongside attack-driven CPU uplift.

After centralized eval, RL encodes fleet state into trust scores; APC combines threat, mission criticality, and resources to choose next-round participation, update cadence, and DP-style noise on weight deltas—balancing IDS accuracy, comms cost, and privacy risk for UAV swarms.
Fraction of predictions matching labels. Intuitive for multi-class IDS but can be skewed by imbalance—pair with macro metrics.
Per-class precision or recall averaged across classes, emphasizing every class matters for intrusion detection.
Standard classification loss; decreasing values usually mean better-calibrated logits, but read together with accuracy.
Heuristic such as 1 − macro_precision fed to APC: lower precision implies a harder or more hostile RF/traffic regime for policy tightening.

Live runs: server.py writes data/live_rounds.json each round; the Dataset tab’s demo accuracy prefers the last centralized eval from that file when present. Otherwise the bundled rounds_en.json snapshot is shown. Trust scores come from RL_module (TrustNet + per-client squashing to ~5–95); see the server console for raw logs.
Strength of DP-style noise injected into uploaded weight deltas; higher protects gradients more but can hurt convergence and accuracy.

participate=0 skips federation this round and returns only global weights, isolating a suspicious node from poisoning the global model. freq_n means allow an uplink at most once every N federated rounds; larger N is sparser. In apc_module, benign/low-threat contexts often keep freq_n=1 (upload every round); under higher threat or low resources it ramps up per rules (up to about 180 in config).
For round r and client id: split_index = (r−1)×3 + id, mapping to data/swarm_processed/train_split_*.npz so each round uses different shards; independent of the geographic theatre labels.
Eval on each drone’s stratified holdout split within its shard; reflects fit on that client’s distribution and may diverge from global test to spot stragglers or anomalies.
